artifacts.summary: Finds none of the four lean-lsp-using lean skills route through skill_preflight_update, so a manifest hooks.preflight declaration (nix's pattern) would be dead code for lean; recommends a direct per-skill Stage 2 call to a new lean-owned wrapper around verify-lean-mcp.sh --quiet, WARN-only, ~30ms measured cost, silent no-op outside a Lean project.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's extension system, a manifest's top-level `hooks.preflight` field (distinct from `provides.hooks`) only fires if the owning extension's skills route Stage 2 through `skill_preflight_update` in skill-base.sh (see context/patterns/skill-preflight-flow.md). Before wiring a new preflight check via that mechanism, grep the extension's own SKILL.md files for `skill_preflight_update` — an extension can declare the hook while its skills silently never reach it (confirmed true for the lean extension as of this task; nix is the one live counter-example).

verify-lean-mcp.sh --quiet against a live ~/.claude.json (~183KB) runs in ~30ms wall clock (jq-only, ~6 sequential jq calls + git rev-parse, no network/repo-walk/server-spawn) -- a useful reference cost figure for 'is this cheap enough for a hot dispatch path' questions involving small-file jq reads.
